reply.shortGloss: to take; to catch; to get
reply.emotion: helpful and ready, reaching out to help someone with something
notes: Prendere is one of the most common verbs in Italian, used for everything from picking up an object to catching a bus or ordering food.
Do not confuse prendere (to take) with portare (to bring/carry), which focuses on moving something toward somewhere else rather than grabbing it.

senses.definition: To get hold of something with your hands and move it or pick it up.

examples.text: Ho deciso di prendere la borsa blu dallo scaffale.
examples.translation: I decided to take the blue bag from the shelf.
examples.emotion: decisive and clear, pointing out a choice made

senses.definition: To take or stop something that is moving towards you, like a ball or a vehicle.

examples.text: Devo correre per prendere l'autobus in orario.
examples.translation: I have to run to catch the bus on time.
examples.emotion: hurried and slightly anxious about missing the time

senses.definition: To order food or a drink in a bar or restaurant.

examples.text: Voglio prendere un caffè prima di iniziare a lavorare.
examples.translation: I want to have a coffee before starting work.
examples.emotion: relaxed and looking forward to a short break
